text.tspan: Furniture, light and space shape an everyday room.
There is more than one way to arrange a room. In my experience, practical preparation and
attention to others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use. For
instance, we keep keys in a bowl beside the door. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over
the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that small personal choices make a space feel familiar. For example, we place
a favourite photograph where we can see it from our chair. This approach recognises that the
experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to
control every detail. We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Compare your first answer with this question: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
